messages:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed a weird perf spike for tenant-42 when we start hitting the fallback chain. route header rewrite from edge appears to be changing lane affinity and sending requests to the low-cost model, which has no warm KV cache so latency jumps.
eric: any repro steps or logs? can you paste an example request/headers? :thinking:
maya: pasted a sanitized example below. header X-Client-Tier is coming from the proxy and then our matcher does a header-override -> route to /v1/generate?model=redwood-lite
---
Request (sanitized):
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Host: api.redwood.example
  X-Client-Tier: enterprise
  X-Route-Override: low-cost
Body: {"prompt":"..."}
---
jamal: so the problem is twofold: (1) header override is applied before affinity lookup, (2) fallback policy has model fallback but not an explicit warmup for KV cache. when capacity is constrained the circuit breaker opens and we immediately drop to the backup model without warming. that explains the latency tail.
sasha: agreed. also we saw similar with quota-driven preemption — requests get demoted then get routed to the cheapest lane which is on slower nodes. we should consider a short warmup path or staged fallback.
eric: propose change: precedence: explicit route header overrides should NOT change lane affinity unless the header is authenticated+approved. default: header-only can suggest a route, but affinity is decided by tenant tag + route match. something like:
```yaml
routing:
  match_order: [tenant_affinity, path, header_suggest]
  header_override:
    allowed: [admin-service, partner-proxy]
    effect: suggest
```
jamal: that looks sane. plus we need fallback policy tweak: when circuit breaker trips, instead of immediate model swap, do staged fallback: try compatible quantized variant on same lane, then fallback lane with a warmup ticket (spawn 1 warm request to populate KV) then shift traffic. pseudo-config:
```json
{"fallback": {"stages": ["same_lane_quant","warm_ticket","lane_shift"]}}
```
maya: nice. small nit: warm_ticket needs to be rate-limited per-tenant to avoid burst costs. also tie warm_ticket to observability so we can see warm success/failure.
sasha: telemetry must add a metric: fallback_warm_success{tenant,route,model} and fallback_latency_delta. console team wants both for rollout UX.
tina: can we run this as a canary on eng-sandbox first? if we change match_order we should be careful — header changes from external proxies could be malicious or misconfigured.
eric: yes. plan: jamal will PR config change with tests + simulation harness; maya + sasha will add telemetry events (warm ticket start/success/failure); tina will coordinate a 10% canary on sandbox tenants for 24h. deploy-bot: please queue canary after PR merge.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: config/route-policy#482 -> canary: eng-sandbox (10%) ETA 12m :rocket:
maya: thanks — I'll collect traces and ping here after 24h. :thumbsup:
